solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stop working because of line in operating system

parts.note: 'it's down to' means it is because of

indicators.note: the line sits in the middle of the operating system's letters

explanation.surface: A computer user stops work because a line of code in the operating system has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside OS to make OLS, after DOWN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To down tools is the idiom for workers stopping or striking.

clue.text: Lady briefly taking you for a Parisian in fact

indicators.note: the shortened title takes the French word into its middle
a word said briefly loses its last letter, so the title is cut short

parts.note: a Dame is a titled lady
tu is the French familiar word for you

explanation.surface: A lady, speaking briefly, uses the French word for you when stating a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the title's last letter, and 'taking' means the shortened lady holds the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a given fact.

clue.text: Book token given by wife — and with it, nothing

indicators.note: the token comes from the wife, so her letter goes first

parts.note: an omen is a sign or token
in means fashionable, with it
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A wife hands over a book token, and with it gives nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: IN as 'with it' is the slang sense of fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in Love is a novel by D. H. Lawrence, so it names a book.

clue.text: Drawing you had coloured a certain way

parts.note: a drawn match is tied, so drawing gives tied
ye'd is an old contraction of you had

explanation.surface: A drawing you made had been coloured in a particular style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' is a game ending level, not a sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dyeing is a dyeing method in which cloth is knotted before colouring.

clue.text: Witness, removed from case, won't peach

indicators.note: taking away the case of the word won't strips its outside letters

parts.note: a peach is an attractive person, a looker

explanation.surface: A witness, dropped from the trial, refuses to inform on anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' in the surface is the old verb meaning to inform; here it is the noun for a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a bystander who sees an event happen, an eyewitness.

clue.text: Narrator's understood the reader's older

indicators.note: what a narrator says is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: understood gives seen and the reader's gives your, the solver's

explanation.surface: A storyteller has grasped that the reader is the elder one.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN YOUR spoken runs together as SENIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior describes someone of greater age or rank than another.

clue.text: One shoe, not quite the pair, going with it

indicators.note: the two pieces go along together side by side

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: both means the two of them, the pair

explanation.surface: Someone has only one shoe, not a full pair, to wear with an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts BOTH to BOT; IT as SA is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a kind of footwear, so one of a pair.

clue.text: Fellow with TV spots royal photographer

parts.note: snow is the speckled interference on an old television screen
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man with spots on a television screen turns out to be a royal photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Snowdon, married to Princess Margaret, was a celebrated photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony Armstrong-Jones, Lord Snowdon, was a photographer married into the royal family.

clue.text: Bachelor place Dorothy visits to see sketch writer

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz travels to the land of Oz

explanation.surface: A bachelor goes where Dorothy went in order to find a writer of sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: Boz was the pen name Dickens used for Sketches by Boz.

clue.text: Once on the outside, we start to work in tandem?

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, worked into a new order
only the outside letters of the word Once are used

explanation.surface: Once we start working, we will be pulling in tandem as a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: OE, the outside of 'Once', joins WE START and 'to work' rearranges all of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem bicycle has places for two riders, so it is one with room for a pair.

clue.text: Run away from anger and depression in Greece

indicators.note: the run is taken away from the angry word

parts.note: temper is anger
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone flees rage and gloom while in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' is a dip in the land, not low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a famous valley in Thessaly, a hollow in the landscape.

clue.text: Ladies, staying on, visit New Zealand tourist attraction

indicators.note: the other pieces stay within the toilet's letters

parts.note: the ladies is a loo
to do a place is to visit it as a tourist

explanation.surface: Women who stay on can visit a New Zealand sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying' signals that the other pieces stay inside the ladies; 'visit' is the tourist's sense of doing a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoo in Regent's Park is a well-known sight that visitors flock to.

clue.text: Easy reward from getting on line?

definitions.text: Easy reward from getting on line?

parts.words: Easy reward from getting on line?
parts.note: getting on means old and a line is a rope, so the payment comes from old rope

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means pay earned for no effort; the question mark flags the punning reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes cash gained for almost no work, an easy reward.

clue.text: A person ends short trip in general store

parts.note: one means a person, as in one should
stops means ends, as a verb
a hop is a short journey

explanation.surface: Someone cuts short a brief journey at a general store.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-stop shop sells everything in one place, like a general store.

clue.text: Laments day-old fails

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
dies means fails, as an engine does

explanation.surface: Someone bewails a day-old failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a poem of mourning sung by one voice, a lament.

clue.text: Painter papers around bottom right corner made ready

parts.note: Claude Monet was the Impressionist painter

indicators.note: the papers go around the corner's letters

parts.note: ID means identity papers
on a map the bottom right corner is south-east, SE

explanation.surface: A painter puts papers around the lower right corner of his canvas to prepare it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash, so made ready means turned into money.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetised means converted into money, and the ready is slang for cash.

clue.text: One outlet accepts new coin

indicators.note: the outer letters take the new letter in

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a vent is an outlet for air

explanation.surface: A shop takes a newly minted coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coin' is the verb, as in coin a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a word or phrase is to make it up, devise it.

clue.text: Leaving possible heir a dodgy business?

parts.note: going means leaving
a son may inherit, so he is a potential heir

explanation.surface: Departing and leaving a likely heir behind looks a suspicious affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Goings-on are suspicious or improper activities, shady affairs.

clue.text: Stupid that hotel do only flipping sandwiches!

definitions.note: a noun here, as in calling someone 'stupid'

indicators.note: the run of letters is flipped to read the other way
the phrase holds the letters wanted within it, like a filling

explanation.surface: An exasperated guest complains that the hotel serves only sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'hotel do only' backwards and ELDOON gives way to the run in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is a slang word for a fool, someone dim-witted.

clue.text: Paranoid old ruler putting Trotsky on trial briefly

indicators.note: Trotsky is put on, that is before, the shortened trial

parts.note: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A paranoid former leader puts Trotsky on a quick trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens TEST to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Leontes is the jealous, suspicious king of Sicilia in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Press chief with another cider, too inebriated!

indicators.note: drunk letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss calls for another cider, though already too drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A coeditor shares the top job at a paper or journal with a colleague.

clue.text: Furniture you'll find in different sorts of theatre

definitions.text: you'll find in different sorts of theatre
definitions.meaning: a ... helps actors dress in a playhouse, and dresses wounds in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: Both a stage theatre and an operating theatre employ a dresser.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a sideboard with shelves, and also a person who helps with costumes or dressings.

clue.text: Challenge on reflection no good: how to go from London to Leeds?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so these letters run backwards

parts.words: how to go from London to Leeds?
parts.note: you go up the M1 motorway, written with I standing in for the 1

explanation.surface: Questioning someone's way north from London to Leeds, on reflection, seems pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway north from London to Leeds, and going north is 'up'. Reflected, NG UP MI gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to dispute or call it into question.

clue.text: New MP, one come to help folk in general

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new MP has arrived to help ordinary voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The common people are the ordinary population, the masses.

clue.text: Retroaction not oddly one to inspire

indicators.note: skipping the odd letters leaves only the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: Acting in reverse, though not strangely, someone serves as a source of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of love poetry, and Muses inspire artists.

clue.text: Fights to finish or to drive out soliciting?

parts.note: shoo means to chase away
touts means solicits custom pushily

explanation.surface: Is it fights to the death, or a way to chase away people soliciting?
explanation.definitionFit: A shootout is a decisive gunfight or penalty contest that settles a match.

clue.text: That's a surprise, the Hoops eclipsing Hearts

indicators.note: the hoops hide the hearts letter between them

parts.note: two hoops are two rings, O and O
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A surprise result as Celtic, the Hoops, overshadow Hearts in Scottish football.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hoops is Celtic's nickname and Hearts is an Edinburgh club, but both are letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Oho is an exclamation of surprise or triumph.

clue.text: Sound unstressed after chief visiting was abused

indicators.note: the chief comes in to stay within the other letters
something abused is mistreated, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: After a visit from the boss, someone sounds calm despite being abused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges the three letters into SWA, and 'visiting' puts the chief's letters inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the neutral vowel heard in unstressed syllables, like the a in about.

clue.text: Refuse when beginning to recycle to break bed down

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the middle of the word for sleeping

parts.note: doss means to sleep rough, bed down

indicators.note: only the start of the word recycle is used

explanation.surface: Rubbish waits to be recycled when someone breaks up a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun meaning rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, rubbish.

clue.text: Moderating playtime instruction often led by ma

definitions.text: Moderating playtime instruction often led by ma

parts.words: Moderating playtime instruction often led by ma
parts.note: a direction for playing music meaning not too much, which often follows ma, but

explanation.walkthrough: 'playtime' means time for playing music, and 'ma' is the Italian for but, as in ma non troppo, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical marking means not too much, a restraining instruction to performers.
